scientific_queries.note: Tests whether the main conclusion depends on the single synergy metric used throughout.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round checks whether the programme's headline claim survives a change of target definition, and it does not.

design.pool: clean unseen-combination pool (the one where C45 found the annotation model losing by 10.12 pp)
design.hit_criterion: top quartile of each metric within the pool

critical_notes.hit_definition_differs_from_C45: C45 used the boolean Synergy flag; this round uses the top quartile of each continuous metric, so it neither reproduces nor contradicts C45
critical_notes.drug_effect_equals_additive_here: marginal = 0.5(a+b)+grand and additive = a+b+grand are monotone transforms, so they rank identically; the round therefore compares drug-effect ranking against the annotation ridge
critical_notes.nothing_significant_under_quartile_crite: all four intervals contain zero, so no metric yields a significant winner

consequence_for_the_headline: the statement 'the annotation model loses to trivial baselines' is restricted to the boolean Synergy criterion and the dAUC metric; under quartile criteria on four continuous metrics nothing is significant and the sign reverses on dEMAX and dXMID
limits: the four metrics are highly correlated, so this is not four independent replications
missingness differs per metric, so pool membership differs slightly
moving to a quartile criterion lowers power (about a quarter of each pool is positive)
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: decide and fix what 'decision value' means before running further experiments, since a free choice of criterion can flip the conclusion

register_updates.C63: new and decisive as a qualification: the main conclusion is metric- and criterion-specific
